area: every candle sits half a bar left of where it belongs
breaks: the bar centre loses its half-bar offset, so the whole series shifts left by half a slot against the axis, the crosshair, the cluster pan and every marker that computes its own x

area: candle bodies touch, so the chart reads as a solid block
breaks: the 0.4 factor is what leaves a gap between adjacent bodies; at 0.5 they abut and a dense chart projected on a wall stops resolving into individual candles

area: a doji disappears
breaks: a bar whose open equals its close has zero body height and vanishes entirely — the minimum of one pixel is the only thing that draws it

area: the wick is drawn from the open and close rather than the high and low
breaks: the wick stops showing the bar's range at all, so the chart understates every excursion — and the sonification, which reads High and Low directly, disagrees with the picture

area: the pixel alignment that keeps wick and body concentric is dropped
breaks: sub-pixel positions return and Skia's anti-aliasing puts the 1px wick a fraction off the body centre on thin-body candles — the asymmetry this line was added to remove

area: the theme stops owning candle colour
breaks: the component's metadata ColorHex — a hardcoded TradingView teal and salmon — overrides the theme again, so every theme repaints the chrome and leaves the candles alone, which is the defect the IsUserStyled test was introduced to end

area: colour-vision-safe mode stops applying
breaks: an accessibility setting a user switched ON does nothing: red/green candles come back for someone who cannot tell them apart

area: hollow up-candles fill in
breaks: the accessibility mode that makes direction readable by SHAPE inverts: down bars are outlined and up bars filled, so shape now says the opposite of colour

area: the two-colour split lands on the wrong side of its baseline
breaks: MFI above its midline paints in the BELOW colour — the exact complaint that produced this code ('I thought it was red below and green above'), inverted

area: a component that never asked for a split gets one
breaks: every component carrying a secondary colour — most of them, for other reasons — starts drawing in two colours split at a baseline it never declared

area: the opt-in area fill becomes opt-out
breaks: the renderer goes back to deciding from the display type, so about twenty-five components that declare IsAreaFill=false start drawing a fill — Cody's explicit call was opt-in

area: the cloud crossover is placed at the wrong point between two bars
breaks: the interpolation that finds where two cloud edges cross uses the wrong end's width, so the bull/bear colour changes at the wrong x and the fill shows a notch at every crossover

area: a marker can swell to cover the bar it annotates
breaks: the clamp that keeps a glyph proportional to the bar spacing widens tenfold, so a high-Thickness marker becomes a blob covering ten bars of chart

area: a marker shrinks below visibility at wide zoom
breaks: the minimum glyph size goes, so on a zoomed-out chart every signal marker collapses to a sub-pixel speck — present in the data, invisible on the screen

area: a bar-anchored marker is drawn at its raw value instead
breaks: BelowBar/AboveBar markers stop following the DISPLAYED bar, so in Heikin-Ashi they float away from the candle they describe and disagree with speech and audio, which follow it

area: the above-bar and below-bar anchors swap
breaks: buy markers sit above the bar and sell markers below it — the single most-read visual convention on the chart, reversed

area: axis labels stop landing on gridlines
breaks: the label step stops being a whole multiple of the gridline step, so labels float between lines — the defect this function was extracted to fix, and the first thing a reviewer notices on a projected chart

area: axis labels crowd on top of one another
breaks: the minimum spacing between labels goes, so a short indicator pane stacks its numbers into an unreadable smear. This mutant SURVIVED the 48th pass's rendering set and is still open

area: the nice-number axis picks arbitrary steps
breaks: the 1/2/5/10 ladder that makes an axis read in round numbers is broken, so a BTC chart labels at 76227.38 again — accurate and useless

area: small panes ask for as many labels as large ones
breaks: a 40px indicator pane asks for five labels it has no room for, which the spacing guard then drops unevenly — the labels that survive are no longer evenly spaced

area: the y-axis swatch becomes a block across the axis
breaks: SKCanvas.DrawRect's four-float overload is (x, y, WIDTH, HEIGHT) — this is the exact confusion recorded in the comment above it, which turned a 4x3 tick into a block burying the axis labels

area: a pane is drawn underneath the x-axis strip
breaks: the panes are laid out as though the x-axis strip were not there, so the bottom pane runs under it — the 2026-09-12 defect where eight panes put the last one off the screen

area: the overflow fit is not applied, so the last pane loses its height
breaks: when saved ratios plus the main pane's floor exceed the canvas, the excess is supposed to be shared across the indicator panes; unshared it all lands on the LAST one, which is drawn off the bottom. Every oscillator has its own pane since 2026-09-11, so this is ordinary

area: the y-axis column is not subtracted from the plot width
breaks: the main pane is drawn under the price axis, so the rightmost bars are hidden behind the labels and every pointer-to-bar mapping — which subtracts the same strip — is off

area: the layout service is told the wrong axis fractions
breaks: every pointer-to-data mapping goes through these two numbers; at zero the click-to-select, the hover readout, Shift+click measurement and every drawing anchor drift across the chart, which is the 2026-08-27 six-bars-out defect restored

area: the divider fractions are reported against the wrong denominator
breaks: the drag handles that resize panes are positioned from these fractions, so every handle sits slightly below its divider and dragging one grabs the wrong pane near the bottom

area: the price axis is upside down
breaks: higher prices map to lower pixels: the entire chart renders vertically mirrored, and every drawing, marker and crosshair with it

area: a degenerate pane range divides by zero instead of centring
breaks: a pane whose min equals its max — a flat series, or one component still in warmup — divides by zero and writes NaN into a coordinate, which Skia turns into nothing drawn at all

area: log scale and linear scale swap
breaks: the log-scale switch inverts, so a linear chart is drawn logarithmically and vice versa — visible immediately on any long-range crypto chart

area: a colour rule matches on the wrong side of its level
breaks: every component using a level-based colour rule paints the two regions the wrong way round

area: a rising bar is coloured as falling
breaks: the direction rules invert, so a rising histogram is painted in the falling colour

area: the first bar of a series is compared against nothing
breaks: the warmup fallback goes from 'compare against itself, so neither rising nor falling' to 'compare against zero', which paints the first visible bar of every negative series as falling and every positive one as rising

area: a phase-coloured candle ignores the phase
breaks: Cipher S's sentiment overlay — the whole point of which is that the candle's colour IS the phase — falls back to ordinary up/down colouring. Grep the test project for `phaseData`: nothing. This branch has never had a fixture

area: a phase overlay draws wicks it is supposed to suppress
breaks: wicks return under a phase overlay and clutter the colour view the overlay exists to give
